title: `mean` of floats: the sum by the count
description: `mean` is the sum (polars-sum-float, pairwise or Kahan by path) divided by the count.

The mean sums in `f64` whatever the input: `_sum_as_f64` (pairwise, `f32` lanes widened to `f64`) ungrouped, `KahanSum<f64>` per index group in memory. A `Float32` mean is that `f64` quotient rounded to `f32`.

Streaming: `NumMeanReducer` keeps an `f64` sum and a count; a morsel adds its `_sum_as_f64`, a grouped row adds itself (`reduce_one`), and pipelines merge by adding sums and counts. So a grouped mean is Kahan in memory and a plain left-to-right `f64` sum when streaming, as for `sum` (polars-sum-float).

Order class (in memory): (a) ungrouped, `_sum_as_f64`: the pairwise kernel per chunk (`Float32` lanes widened exactly to `f64`), chunks added in turn, then one division by the count; index-grouped, Kahan in `f64`, then the division; a `Float32` mean rounds the `f64` quotient to `f32`. (b) Pairwise: γ_{h+1} Σ|x_i| / n with h as in polars-sum-float (Higham §4.2); Kahan: (2u + O(nu²)) Σ|x_i| / n plus the quotient's u (§4.3); u = 2⁻⁵³; the `Float32` result adds one rounding at 2⁻²⁴. (c) The source below; s-group-mean-cancel (0.5 in memory). (d) Ungrouped `Float64`: ANY. Grouped (Kahan): no Lean order. `Float32`: the sum refines ANY on the widened values, but the final rounding to `f32` is outside `AggFn.avg`, which returns the double quotient.
